quest.title: Heart of the Machine
quest.description: The mechanical crab has stopped at a certain point. The source of the contamination seems to be within.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kuli...

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kuli...

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It stopped here!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Upon closer inspection, the plants here are really different.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ley Line energies are also stronger here. This may be the place we've been looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ready yourselves. We're going in.

talks.objective: Defeat the mechanical monsters that lurk here

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this?

choices.text: I've never seen a machine like this before...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ley Line energy is spilling out from here.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: This device... It's extracting energy from the Ley Lines without end.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Who in the world would do this without considering the consequences? The Ley Lines won't be able to repair themselves if their flow is perpetually disrupted like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's terrible... We have to stop it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... Ugh, Paimon doesn't see controls anywhere!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm starting to get dizzy...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Standing here is equivalent to being directly showered in Ley Line energy, which may cause irreversible damage to your body.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, take Paimon and get out of here. I'll see if I can find a way to turn this thing off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... You're also vulnerable to the Ley Lines, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're staying. We can't leave you here by yourself!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Then let's look for it together. If there is no control unit here, then there must be a "trapdoor" somewhere—

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kolu!

response.speaker: Mechanical Crab
response.text: Kalu! Kalu!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know where it is? Hey, wait for us!

talks.objective: Follow the mechanical crab and continue your search
Check on the person who has collapsed

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! Someone's here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you the one that's taking the Ley Lines' energy? Turn off that machine now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why aren't you saying anything? Too ashamed?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...His body is cold.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's emaciated, and his eyes are sunken, likely from chronic malnourishment and stress. He collapsed and never got back up. What exactly happened here?

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Almost forgot about you. Here, this is the last one.

dialogues.speaker: Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: Kalu! Kalu!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it doing?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm not sure. Judging by this room's layout, this place was a laboratory. We should find a repository of research documents if we keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The file room will definitely give us some clues, so let's go take a look. Maybe we can piece together what happened here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you two find anything?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: There are a lot of lab notes, but it would take way too long to read through them all. I found a tape recording used for an experiment, and based on its serial number, it's from two years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tape recording?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes. The Spantamad created a device that visually records experiments and consolidates the final production into a tape.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: However, these devices are expensive to make and aren't entirely stable. That's why they are only used in some laboratories and do not see wider usage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's watch it!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hold on, let me figure out how to play the tape. Okay, this should do it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After inserting the tape, the projector gradually begins to display a recording of the past...
Karkata? Karkata? Seriously, I look away for one second and you're gone?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?
There you are! Look here — this is our new home!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: I, Abattouy, will unleash my talents here and amaze those ancient fossils at the Akademiya!

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Oh? You're also quite happy! Karkata, do you know what we're about to do?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Yes, I thought not.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Listen up, Karkata. I'm going to make a mechanical life form that can be mass-produced. The technology will be unlike anything else that exists.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: I'll use mechanical organs, and electric currents will course through them like blood. A steel-cast heart that will beat forever, and a brain of myriad components that can think like mine.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Inspiration from the ruins, and the research that the Akademiya had banned... I hope everything can start anew from this place.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: When you can understand our language and live among us, you will no longer be a boring machine, but a truly living being!

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: It's fine. You will understand. One day, you will understand me...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The recording ends here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Karkata is the mechanical crab, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And that researcher named Abattouy said he wanted to prove something to the Akademiya?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Banned research...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I remember now. I had a junior researcher named Abattouy. He was expelled from the Akademiya for researching mechanical life forms.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Junior researcher"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Junior researcher"?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yeah, what's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Nothing, Paimon was just wondering... Doesn't Abattouy look older than you?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: He is, but academic progression isn't tied to age. I finished my studies a while ago, so subsequent students generally considered me as their senior.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Of course, age can be an issue. For a while, people always dragged me into pictures. I felt like some kind of animal on display...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Ahem, that isn't important. Let's go and see if we can find other tape recordings.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, look! Paimon found another tape!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A date is written on it! Let Paimon see... It's from half a year ago!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: That's quite the time gap. I wonder what happened in between...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After inserting the tape, the projector gradually begins to display a recording of the past...

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: It's rare that you malfunction because of an operational error.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Seems that making coffee is still somewhat difficult for you. Or is there an issue with my set parameters?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kuli...

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Alright, there you go.

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Water entered the chela and caused it to short-circuit, so it couldn't receive signals from the ganglion...

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Look at me, talking to you like this. You can't understand me anyway, can you? It's fine. I swapped in some new parts, so you should be alright now.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Try moving around. Everything in working order?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Be more careful next time! We're tight on money right now, so we don't have a lot of parts or power to spare.

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: I'm glad. Karkata, did you know? Yesterday, I dreamed that you could talk.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Aren't the bunch at the Akademiya always saying things like "mechanical intelligence is just an extension of statistics"? They were blown away when they saw us talking with each other.

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Too bad it was just a dream. Forget holding a conversation with me — you're so simple that you probably wouldn't even notice if I died.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Never mind, I should probably be worrying about next month's power...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The recording ends here.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: After Abattouy left the Akademiya, everyone lost contact with him.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I thought he was so despondent that he gave up on researching mechanical life forms. Instead, he had holed up here and continued his experiments.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't feel like he's a bad person. He even changed out Karkata's broken parts. Why would he mess with Ley Lines?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He mentioned something about "power."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let's keep looking around.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Following the serial numbers, the next recording should be here.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The writing is sloppy. Perhaps his state of mind had changed.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: There's also an undated tape in the wrong spot. It doesn't seem like Abattouy put it there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe Karkata helped him with sorting?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's hard to say. These are the last two tape recordings. Let's watch them.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After inserting the tape, the projector gradually begins to display a recording of the past...

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kuli...

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Sorry, Karkata. I was just thinking about something. Today might become a special day.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: In my recent experiments, I successfully gave you a living being's "instincts."

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: When you're low on power or if one of your parts is damaged, you will prioritize your "survival" command and proactively recharge or replace your parts.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: That is a very dangerous thing. And today, I did something even more dangerous.

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: I've officially activated the third generation Ley Line Extractor. The Ley Lines will serve as our power source from now on.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Conducting research on mechanical life forms requires a large amount of power. Even if I scrimped and saved, the Mora I have wouldn't last for long.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: I'm also getting tired, Karkata. I don't know what's driving me to continue with this research anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: They say that even if it simulates the operation of a living creature's organs, a machine is still an ice-cold tool. I want to prove them wrong. I want to turn you into a living, breathing, and talking being...

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: I'm not talking about anything cheerful, Karkata.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Modules for language, emotion, and movement... I've been working my absolute hardest to augment and refine your functionalities, but I've never seen an effective response.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: You are my finest success, but even you can't understand me. All you can do is execute limited responses based on preset commands or keywords.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Karkata, I wish you could speak to me, even just once...

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: *sigh* Yes. You cannot understand me, so you cannot answer me, either.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: It is what it is. In a few days, I'll sell the failed Ley Line Extractor for some Mora and continue my experiments. Life goes on, and I have to as well — I don't have any other choice.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The recording ends here. Tighnari quietly inserts the next tape.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: This is new.

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: If I place another two control modules here to simulate the brain's thalamus...

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Agh... Of course my heart decides to act up now. Why did I cut medication from our expenses...? Karkata? Come help me— *cough*

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Strange... I feel weak...

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Oh no, I have to shut down the extractor...

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Shut them off... *cough* *cough* If we let them recharge indefinitely... they'll... go out of control...

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: Right... I never input a command to shut down the extractor, so you don't understand what I'm saying...

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: In the end, it's just like the Akademiya said: Mechanical life forms only bring danger. My research... Was there any point to it at all?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kulilu?

dialogues.speaker: Karkata
dialogues.text: Kolu!

dialogues.speaker: Abattouy
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, Karkata... In the end, I still wasn't able to turn you... into a true mechanical life form...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The last recording ends here.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I see, so the Ley Line effluence was an accident.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: After Abattouy's unexpected death, the mechanical monsters were driven by their "instincts" and continuously drew out power from the Ley Line Extractor. This eventually resulted in severe damage to the Ley Lines.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then, Karkata...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon understands, then why didn't Karkata go haywire like the other machines?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Because Karkata is different from the other machines.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: To Abattouy, for a machine to truly be considered a mechanical life form, it must possess features similar to any other living organism... It should be structured similarly, it must be able to cry and laugh, and it must have the capacity for independent thought...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Perhaps only by building such a machine could he have the Akademiya acknowledge his protracted research.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But if he had slowed down and saw Karkata as a friend instead of as an experimental product, he would have noticed.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Karkata can't speak, and yet it cares about Abattouy far more than it does about itself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You'll see in a bit. But before that, we have a more urgent task at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: First, let's find the control unit for the Ley Line Extractor and shut it down.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...This should be the control unit.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Once we turn it off, the Ley Line Extractor should also shut down.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Without an external force damaging the Ley Lines, they should start to slowly repair themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, but I bet you two are more worried about Karkata. Let's head back.

dialogues.speaker: Lab Scene
dialogues.text: (Before you lies a non-operational Karkata and a lifeless Abattouy.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... Karkata has been collecting parts because it thinks doing so will "fix" its owner?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Karkata is unable to understand the concept of "death."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: However, it probably remembers when Abattouy replaced its parts when it malfunctioned, and how that restored it to an operational state.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's true that Karkata isn't able to think or understand many topics, but it is like a small child that imitates what adults do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's why it kept stealing mechanical parts... But, it can't repair its owner, no matter how hard it tries.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, but the important thing is that it formed the thought of "wanting to repair Abattouy."

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Who knows how this thought came to be... but it has even suppressed the "instincts" that Abattouy had installed.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If it really is as we've predicted, this research truly will make waves in the Akademiya. It might've been possible to achieve this with ancient technology, but no one has been able to do the same with modern tools.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Karkata? Karkata?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can you hear Paimon? Tighnari says you're awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's not responding...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It reached its limit. It hasn't recharged this entire time, nor has it replaced its severely damaged parts.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's truly a miracle that it managed to hang on for so long.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm going to go confirm that the Ley Line Extractor has shut down. Come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Let them... be alone for a while.

talks.objective: Check on the Ley Line Extractor

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: The Ley Line Extractor has ceased operations.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Traces of Ley Line energy are still in the atmosphere, but the effluence's source has been stopped. The Purification Devices will handle the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Moving on, those affected by the Ley Lines need immediate care. We'll put up an announcement on the bulletin board about the dangers of entering the contaminated region, and for symptomatic individuals to find Collei.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: According to the Akademiya's policies, we need to bring everything back.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Research materials related to mechanical life forms will be destroyed, and Karkata will be disassembled and sealed away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What the heck!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: You two should return first. I'll take care of things here.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Although we've stopped the source of the effluence, the Ley Line energy in the air exceeds normal values. Your bodies won't be able to hold up if you continue to stay here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: #Listen, {NICKNAME} hasn't rested very well, right?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Also, it'll take some time to pack up all the research documents. You're not familiar with this research after all, so you won't be of much use here.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Tell the Adventurers' Guild that the incident has been resolved, and then get some sleep. We can discuss matters tomorrow.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tighnari marks out Pardis Dhyai on the map. He usually goes there when doing research.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Oh, and... Don't talk about Abattouy. The fewer that know about mechanical life form research, the better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright... Then, let's go back to Katheryne...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Why are you still here?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'll take care of this. Go and report to the Adventurers' Guild, and then get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Observe Karkata
dialogues.text: (Karkata stands in front of the machine, as if thinking about something.)

dialogues.speaker: Observe Mechanical Crab
dialogues.text: (The mechanical crab stands in front of the machine, as if thinking about something.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a ton of mechanical monsters here! They made this place their lair!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Looks like there's no way to sneak by. Let's take care of them quickly.
